system.name: Tempo
system.one_liner: a deep learning system that compiles a declarative, recurrent-tensor program into a whole-program-optimized schedule via a symbolic dependence graph

content.subject: how Tempo turns a logical-time dependency graph into ILP constraints, solves for a schedule, and scans it into an AST

elements.name: x
elements.role: the input tensor's nodes, one per logical timestep t=0..7

elements.name: y
elements.role: the output tensor's nodes, each depending on a window of x (t to min(t+3,T))

elements.name: Domain
elements.role: constraint bounding x[t] and y[t] to 0<=t<T=8

elements.name: Validity
elements.role: constraint giving the dependency range x[t:min(t+3,T)] -> y[t]

elements.name: Proximity
elements.role: objective term x[min(t+3,T)] -> y[t] guiding the scheduler toward temporal locality

elements.name: θ
elements.role: the schedule function solved by the ILP, shown skewing nodes from Domain into Schedule

elements.name: for c0 in 0...10
elements.role: AST root loop scanning every execution-time step, marked as 'happens-before' sequential

elements.name: sequence
elements.role: AST node enforcing the happens-before order of the loop body

elements.name: if c0<=7
elements.role: AST branch guarding when x is executed

elements.name: if c0>=3
elements.role: AST branch guarding when y is executed

elements.name: exec x[c0]
elements.role: AST leaf executing x at the current loop index

elements.name: exec y[c0-3]
elements.role: AST leaf executing y, reading the shifted index c0-3

relations.what: y[t] depends on the window x[t:min(t+3,T)]
the SDG's domain/validity/proximity are read off directly as polyhedral constraints
solving the ILP over these constraints yields a schedule function theta
applying theta skews each node from its logical-time position to an execution-time position, delaying y by 3 steps
scanning the schedule produces the imperative AST's loop and branch structure

panels.label: Domain (Logical Time)
panels.differs: template/first frame: x and y nodes positioned by logical time t=0..7 (T-1=7), with dependency arrows still in their original, unscheduled order

panels.label: Schedule (Execution Time)
panels.differs: the same x/y nodes repositioned by the solved schedule function theta into execution-time slots 0..9, delaying y's execution by 3 steps relative to x

content.key_idea: Tempo turns a symbolic dependency graph's domain and validity/proximity constraints into an integer linear program, solves it for a schedule function theta that reorders nodes from logical to execution time, and scans that schedule into a branching imperative loop.
content.reading_order: top-left Domain graph, right to the Constraints box (1), down to Solve ILP (2) and the theta-skewed Schedule graph (3), then right to the AST (4)

encoding.color_means: blue marks x nodes/labels and green marks y nodes/labels throughout; red highlights one specific dependency edge so the reader can track how its shape changes from the Domain graph to the Schedule graph
encoding.line_style_means: thin gray arrows are ordinary x-to-y dependencies; the same edge recoloured red in both graphs traces one concrete example dependency before and after scheduling
encoding.state_means: the Domain (Logical Time) and Schedule (Execution Time) graphs are the same x/y node set before and after applying the solved schedule function theta, so node identity (colour, row) stays fixed while only horizontal position shifts
encoding.marker_means: circled numbers 1-4 order the pipeline: turning the SDG into constraints, solving the ILP, obtaining the schedule (theta), and scanning it into an AST
encoding.emphasis: the red-highlighted edge and the visible rightward skew of y's nodes between the Domain and Schedule graphs make the 3-step scheduling delay directly visible, not just stated in the constraint text
reusable_patterns: a before/after node-link graph pair (skewed by a solved transform) flanked by the formal constraints that produced it and the code artifact it compiles to, tied together by a numbered pipeline
weaknesses: the theta label marking step 3 is small and sits between the two graphs without its own arrow, so its role as 'the solved schedule being applied' is easy to miss versus the numbered 1/2/4 steps

sections: §5 Scheduling SDGs with the Polyhedral Model
evidence: Fig. 14 shows the scheduling approach in Tempo
Tempo stores the resulting schedule function
We describe how Tempo scans the schedule to produce an imperative program AST

summary: Figure 14 shows how Tempo schedules the example y[t] = f(x[t:min(t+3,T)]) with T=8. The Domain (Logical Time) graph draws x and y as two rows of nodes indexed 0 to T-1=7, with gray dependency arrows (one highlighted red) linking each y[t] to its x window. Step 1 reads this SDG directly into Domain, Validity, and Proximity polyhedral constraints. Step 2 solves an ILP over those constraints (via the Pluto scheduler) to find a schedule function theta; applying it (3) skews the same x/y nodes into the Schedule (Execution Time) graph, delaying y's execution by 3 steps relative to x, shown by the same red edge now spanning further right. Step 4 scans this schedule into an imperative AST: a 'for c0 in 0...10' loop whose happens-before sequence branches into 'if c0<=7: exec x[c0]' and 'if c0>=3: exec y[c0-3]'.
